title: Counting by level
description:
Write a handler class `CountingHandler(logging.Handler)` that a program can attach to see how it is doing:

- `counts` is a dictionary from level name (`"INFO"`, `"ERROR"` ...) to how many records of that level were handled;
- `last(n)` returns the last `n` messages (finished text from `record.getMessage()`, newest last), keeping at most 100 overall;
- `errors()` returns the messages of every `ERROR` and `CRITICAL` record still kept, oldest first;
- it respects its own level: `CountingHandler(level=logging.WARNING)` ignores `INFO` records (the `logging` module does this for you if you call the parent constructor).

```python
h = CountingHandler()
log = logging.getLogger("app"); log.setLevel(logging.DEBUG); log.addHandler(h)
log.info("start"); log.error("disk %s", "full")
print(h.counts, h.last(1), h.errors())   # {'INFO': 1, 'ERROR': 1} ['disk full'] ['disk full']
```
hints: Call `super().__init__(level)` in your constructor: the base class stores the level and only calls `emit` for records at or above it.
`collections.deque(maxlen=100)` drops the oldest item by itself when a new one arrives; store `(record.levelno, record.getMessage())` pairs so `errors()` can filter by level.
unitTests:
import logging

def fresh(name, handler):
    log = logging.getLogger(name)
    log.handlers.clear()
    log.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
    log.propagate = False
    log.addHandler(handler)
    return log

@test("counts per level")
def _():
    h = CountingHandler()
    log = fresh("c.one", h)
    log.info("a"); log.info("b"); log.error("c")
    check_eq(h.counts, {"INFO": 2, "ERROR": 1})

@test("last gives finished messages, newest last")
def _():
    h = CountingHandler()
    log = fresh("c.two", h)
    log.info("start"); log.warning("disk %s", "full")
    check_eq(h.last(1), ["disk full"])
    check_eq(h.last(5), ["start", "disk full"])
    check_eq(h.last(0), [])

@test("errors keeps ERROR and CRITICAL only")
def _():
    h = CountingHandler()
    log = fresh("c.three", h)
    log.info("i"); log.error("e1"); log.critical("c1"); log.warning("w")
    check_eq(h.errors(), ["e1", "c1"])

@test("keeps at most 100 messages")
def _():
    h = CountingHandler()
    log = fresh("c.four", h)
    for i in range(150):
        log.info("m%d", i)
    check_eq(len(h.last(1000)), 100)
    check_eq(h.last(1), ["m149"])
    check_eq(h.counts["INFO"], 150)

@test("its own level filters records")
def _():
    h = CountingHandler(level=logging.WARNING)
    log = fresh("c.five", h)
    log.info("hidden"); log.warning("shown")
    check_eq(h.counts, {"WARNING": 1})
